absent: Standard sheaf capacity default and barn full and empty limit values.
Barn acquisition and insertion and retrieval plus empty sheaf allocation and release implementations.
Sheaf flush and refill and pfmemalloc prefill plus per CPU bulk refill implementations.
Full layouts and locking of cache and node and slab and page structures beyond observed fields.
Numeric values and semantics of allocation and slab flags and node constants and page order limits.
Slab hook and trace and fencing and sanitizer and accounting behaviors beyond call sites shown.
RCU grace and irq work scheduling guarantees for deferred free paths.
Allocation statistic counter definitions and export interface.
Zero size pointer definition and usable size query implementation.
Vmalloc range allocation and vmalloc realloc behaviors for vmalloc backed objects.

findings.text: Sheaf batch interface provides acquisition of a populated sheaf for a requested count, return of a used sheaf for reuse or disposal, growth of an existing sheaf to a larger count, single object removal from a sheaf, and query of current fill count.

General sized allocation family offers large object allocation, node aware allocation, node unaware allocation, nolock allocation, caller tracked allocation, and cache specified allocation with and without node selection.
Bulk cache allocation comprises a public wrapper that reports overall success and an internal helper that either fills the whole output range or releases partial progress and reports failure.

Resizing and mixed allocator interface provides node aligned realloc, node aware kvmalloc with vmalloc fallback, atomic free dispatch, sensitive free with clearing, node aligned kvrealloc with fallback, and an RCU callback for deferred kvfree.
Inspection and release helpers provide a test for whether a cache has no active slabs on any node, a usercopy range validator for heap objects, and a direct single object free path with accounting.
Boot parameter handlers accept minimum and maximum slab order values and a no argument strict NUMA switch, each registered through a parameter operations structure.

Deferred execution entry points comprise an irq work handler draining three pending lists, an RCU handler disposing a sheaf, a debug RCU handler resuming a delayed slab free, and an RCU handler completing a kvfree.
Detached freelist aggregates a slab reference, a tail pointer, a head pointer, an element count, and a cache reference for batched free list handling.

Sheaf state observed across uses includes a capacity limit, a current fill count, an object pointer storage area, a pfmemalloc marker, a back pointer to the owning cache, a node identifier, an RCU head, and a lockless list node.
Per CPU sheaf caching uses a spare sheaf slot guarded by a local lock, while a per node barn tracks counts of stored full sheaves and stored empty sheaves.
Allocation context carries a caller address, an original request size, and an allocation behavior flag distinguishing default locking from nolock operation.
Deferred per CPU work bundles a work item with three separate lockless lists for plain objects awaiting free, objects awaiting RCU based kvfree, and sheaves awaiting RCU based disposal.

Prefill with zero count yields no sheaf. Oversize requests beyond standard capacity yield a dedicated sheaf sized to the request that is either fully populated or discarded. Standard requests reuse a spare or barn sheaf when available, normalize capacity and clear pfmemalloc marking, and discard sheaves found to retain pfmemalloc content.

Return of a sheaf whose capacity differs from standard capacity or which is marked pfmemalloc always flushes unused objects and releases the empty container. Standard clean sheaves prefer the spare slot, otherwise require an available barn below the full limit plus successful refill before barn insertion, else flush and release.

Refill rejects missing handle arguments and reports success when current fill already satisfies the request. Growth within capacity refills in place using a pfmemalloc aware path for standard capacity and a bulk path otherwise. Growth beyond capacity replaces the handle with a newly prefilled sheaf and returns the old one.

Single allocation from a sheaf fails gracefully when empty, otherwise prefers a fenced allocation when available and falls back to removing the most recently stored object. Post allocation accounting and tracing apply to the outcome, and the size query reflects live fill count.

Internal bulk allocation is all or nothing: tiny or debug caches allocate singly with free pointer sanitization, other caches use a batched refill with slowpath accounting, and any shortfall releases what was obtained. The public wrapper rejects empty requests, honors pre allocation failure, allows at most one fenced object placed at a random position, combines fast per CPU bulk with slow bulk, and unwinds both plus the fenced object on failure.

Reallocation treats null or zero pointers as fresh allocation, fails on failed integrity byte check, discovers usable size differently for fenced, slab, and large objects, forces fresh allocation on node mismatch when node constrained, reuses in place when new size fits and alignment holds with zeroing of changed span and redzone upkeep, otherwise allocates anew and copies the smaller of new size and old usable size.

Node aligned realloc wrapper frees its input and yields a zero size pointer when new size is zero, otherwise delegates reallocation and releases the old object only when old and new tagged addresses differ.

Allocation flag adjustment for larger than page requests adds a no warning behavior, suppresses direct reclaim unless retry mayfail is present, and removes nofail reliance on vmalloc fallback. Kvmalloc first attempts the adjusted kmalloc and returns on success or for page sized or smaller requests, rejects excessively large sizes, and otherwise uses a vmalloc range with huge mapping allowed only when blocking is permitted.

Kvrealloc directs vmalloc sourced pointers to a vmalloc realloc path. Other pointers first attempt krealloc with adjusted flags; if that fails it attempts kvmalloc, copies the smaller of requested size and old usable size when an old object exists, releases the old object, and reports failure only if the fallback also fails.

Atomic free dispatches on vmalloc address classification. Sensitive free ignores null or zero pointers and otherwise clears the given length before general free. The RCU free callback releases vmalloc objects through vmalloc release, slab objects through slab free, and large kmalloc objects through large release.

RCU sheaf disposal flushes everything when preparation reports pfmemalloc presence or when no barn exists for the sheaf node, treats debug induced empty sheaves as empty candidates, inserts into the full set when below limit, otherwise flushes then inserts into the empty set when below limit, else releases the empty container.

Deferred work drains each pending list independently: plain objects are mapped to slab and cache with start adjustment and free pointer clearing before slow free, RCU bound allocations are forwarded to an RCU based kvmalloc free helper, and pending sheaves are scheduled through RCU.

A cache counts as empty only when every node has no partial slabs and no slabs overall. Heap usercopy validation rejects pointers below the slab base, derives intra object offset with a fenced special case, rejects left redzone membership, and permits only ranges fully inside the configured user offset window, otherwise aborts.

Minimum order parsing propagates conversion failure and raises maximum when minimum exceeds it. Maximum order parsing propagates failure, caps at the global page order limit, and lowers minimum when minimum exceeds it. Strict NUMA activation applies only on multi node systems and otherwise warns.

Access to the per CPU spare sheaf slot and the associated barn lookup during prefill and return is serialized by a per cache local lock, released before potentially blocking empty container allocation or barn insertion and final disposal.
Barn full and empty occupancy checks use intentionally racy reads outside the barn lock to avoid contention at limits, accepting rare transient overshoot as harmless.

Sheaf objects move among unallocated, empty, partially filled, full, per CPU spare, barn full, barn empty, oversize dedicated, pfmemalloc contaminated, RCU pending, and flushed released states, with oversize and contaminated outcomes forced toward flush and release rather than barn reuse.
Mixed allocation moves from adjusted kmalloc attempt to immediate success, to size based rejection, to vmalloc fallback with blocking dependent mapping options, to final success or failure.

Integrity hazards include reuse after free detected during realloc, redzone and usercopy window violations aborting the copy, use of fenced addresses or missing slabs or non typesafe caches in debug RCU free paths triggering warnings, and large object size and address invariant violations.

Resource hazards include barn overfill beyond configured full and empty limits, retention of pfmemalloc backed objects in reusable sheaves, partial bulk results leaking without unwind, and oversize sheaves entering barn reuse instead of flush and release.
Shrink promotion bound is thirty two.

Direct cache free maps the pointer to its slab and releases a single object with slowpath accounting. Debug RCU delayed free releases its descriptor first, validates fenced address absence plus slab presence plus typesafe flag, then conditionally resumes slow free based on the free hook outcome.

Sized allocation variants share a common delegation shape differing only in supplied node, caller identity, original size, and default versus nolock behavior, with cache variants adding tracing and sanitizer handling and the large variant deriving order from size for tracing.
